messages:
Ava: Quick thread / planning: we need a lean battlecard + SDR one-pager and inbound routing rules for the May launch. Focus: concise competitor knockdowns vs CloudX, LLMAPI, and InfraCo. Timebox = today. :stopwatch:

Tom: I'll own the battlecard bullets. Suggest 3 axes: economics (unit cost predictability), ops (rollouts & fallbacks), dev DX (same API across deploy modes). Keep soundbites <20 words.

Priya: For SDR one-pager: 2-line opener, 3 pain points + rebut lines, qualifying Qs, and routing hints. Drafting now.

Sam: Ops, can we implement staged routing rules that tag leads by intent so SDRs can prioritize benchmarks/latency leads? Example patterns below.

OpsBot: Yes. Provide regex groups and target queues. We log original message and match score.

Sam: ```
# routing prototype
rules:
  - id: bench_intent
    pattern: ".*benchmark|latency|p95|throughput|cost per token"
    queue: sdr-bench
  - id: enterprise_sla
    pattern: ".*SLA|enterprise|private deployment|VPC|dedicated"
    queue: ae-enterprise
  - id: compliance
    pattern: ".*on-prem|air-gapped|HSM|HIPAA|SOC 2"
    queue: solutions
```

bench-bot: benchmark upload completed (2026-05-02). Key soundbites: "20% lower p50 vs CloudX on dedicated pools", "predictable unit economics at scale (batching+cache)". Methodology link: https://drive.redwood/benchmarks/2026-may. Include config caveats.

Priya: Note: flag every claim with a one-line methodology caveat on the one-pager: e.g., "measured on dedicated pool, quantization Q3, standard seq=2k". Legal wants that.

Ava: Battlecard competitor lines (first pass):
- CloudX: "Wide model catalog, but pricing volatility and single-tenant routing gaps." -> Rebut: "Unified runtime that preserves SLAs across hosted/dedicated/private; explicit fallback policies."
- LLMAPI: "Simple API access, no deployment parity or observability." -> Rebut: "Same API surface with rollout controls, token-level cost + latency breakdowns."
- InfraCo: "Bring-your-own infra, ops burden." -> Rebut: "Managed inference runtime + migration playbook; optional private plane for regulated customers."

Tom: Love it. Add 2 short objection scripts for "we're on CloudX already" and "we self-host with infra vendor". Each should be 1-2 sentences.

Priya: Drafts:
- CloudX objection: "Totally valid. Many customers start there; we help reduce unit cost variance and give predictable latency by offloading serving complexities (batching, cache 1) so engineering can focus on product."
- InfraCo objection: "If you're self-hosted, our private deployment lets you keep network controls while getting a runtime tuned for production LLM economics 1 migration assistance included."

Sam: For webinar soundbites, we need p50/p95 and a small chart talking point. Also a one-liner for intro slide: "Ship LLM features with production economics: predictable latency, lower ops toil."

Ava: Marketing ops items: create invite A/B tests (subject lines), update routing config in staging, attach battlecard + one-pager to webinar invite for SDRs.

OpsBot: Routing pushed to staging at 11:30 PT. Will auto-promote to prod after 24h smoke if no high-match false positives. Logs: https://ops.redwood/routing-logs/1763812345

Tom: Subject lines (proposed): 1) "How we cut inference variance and kept latency predictable" 2) "Build LLM features that meet production SLAs"  vote?

Priya: 2 for subject 2. It's clearer for execs.

Ava: Action items: @Tom finalize battlecard bullets by 14:00, @Priya finish SDR one-pager + objection scripts by 15:00, @Sam confirm routing in prod after smoke window, @OpsBot keep logs and send anomaly alerts. We'll review copy in the 15:30 sync. Thanks :sparkles:
